h1: A beloved language app with real usability problems. So I redesigned it.
h3:
Busuu has millions of users — but a heuristic evaluation revealed friction points that were quietly pushing people away. The onboarding dropped users directly into a lesson with no way out. The tab bar lacked labels, making navigation confusing. Progress felt invisible. Videos were too small for mobile screens. No incentives to keep going.
My redesign tackled all of this: a clearer tab bar with named sections and intuitive icons, a more visible progress bar, a quick-access dictionary, and an onboarding flow that actually welcomes users before throwing them into content. The result? Testers found it modern, easy to navigate, and intuitive — completing most tasks successfully on the first try. One small but meaningful win: switching the active tab indicator from a moving line to filled icons + bold labels made location instantly obvious.

Testers loved the home and navigation — and asked for more. The Community and Profile sections are next on my list, along with deeper support for users while they're actively learning. Good design is never finished, just iterated.

h1: Because finding the perfect spot to shoot shouldn't take longer than the shoot itself.
h2: Want to see how it all came together?
h3:
Filmo acá is a mobile app that helps cinematographers, photographers, and small production teams find and book locations — with all the details they actually need to decide, in one place. Real users validated the architecture through card sorting: 90% grouped categories the same way. 100% of testers searched from the home screen without help. The booking flow went from confusing to 5 simple steps.
Three things I'm proud of:
✓ Real users validated the information architecture through card sorting. 90% grouped categories the same way — that's not a guess, that's a pattern.
✓ 100% of testers could search from the home screen without help. That's the kind of clarity you design for.
✓ The booking flow went from "how do I do this?" to 5 simple steps. Log in, search, filter, check availability, book.
The full process is on Behance — research, wireframes, usability testing, satisfaction metrics, and the complete UI redesign.

h1: InnFlow — Personalized Fitness That Adapts to You.
h2: A More Flexible Fitness Experience' Solution
h3: A fitness app that tailors training sessions based on users' preferences, environment, and available equipment, while encouraging connection through community workouts. InnFlow is an app that tailors training sessions according to users' preferences, offering personalized classes based on their needs. It provides recommendations on nutrition, relaxation, muscle activation, intensity, and the difficulty level of each practice. It also offers the option to customize each training session based on the tools available to you and whether you are indoors or outdoors, such as in a square or a park. It has a premium membership that allows users to connect with others nearby, offering the possibility of meeting up and engaging in group physical activities.

InnFlow is a personalized fitness platform that creates training sessions tailored to each user. The app recommends workouts based on preferences, intensity level, location (indoor or outdoor), and available equipment. It also integrates guidance on nutrition, muscle activation, relaxation, and difficulty level to support a more holistic fitness experience. 

Feature 1 — Personalized Training
Workouts adapt to the user's preferences, goals, and energy level.

Feature 2 — Environment-Based Workouts
Training sessions adjust depending on whether users are indoors or outdoors, such as at home, in a park, or in a public space.

Feature 3 — Equipment Flexibility
Users can customize sessions based on the tools they have available.

Feature 4 — Community Connection
Premium users can connect with people nearby and organize group training sessions.

/projects/cashfly.description: Product Designer & UX/UI Specialist with 5+ years of experience crafting clear and intuitive digital experiences.
h1: Young people want to invest. The existing tools make it feel impossible.
h3:
CashFly is a fintech web app designed for young people who are just getting started with investing and personal loans. Built on John Maeda's Laws of Simplicity, every decision was made to reduce cognitive load and make finance feel approachable.
Through user research we found that the biggest barrier wasn't money — it was confusion. Too many options, too much jargon, no guidance. So we scoped the MVP down to four core actions: sign up, log in, request a loan, and invest. This constraint was the product.
I led the end-to-end design process — user research, user flows, wireframes, UI design, interactive prototype, and usability testing.

By removing everything non-essential, we created space for confidence. CashFly gives first-time investors a clean, focused experience — no overwhelm, no jargon, just the tools they actually need to get started.
